read.title: Read
read.heading: Books and chapters translated so far
read.dek: Each passage is translated from the Hebrew of the Westminster Leningrad Codex or the SBL Greek New Testament at three levels, with the reasoning behind every sentence. English comes first; Spanish, French, Swahili, Vietnamese and Korean follow, and where a sentence is not yet in your language the reader shows the English. All are AI-assisted, and none is marked reviewed until a reviewer who reads Hebrew or Greek approves it.
read.step1: Choose how it reads. Literal, Balanced or Readable, and your wording settings: inclusive or traditional language, “Christ” or “Messiah”, he or He.
read.step2: Tap any verse. The Greek appears with a word-for-word gloss beside the translation.
read.step3: See every decision. What the original means, what else was considered, why this wording was chosen, and which calls are uncertain.

beliefs.title: What we believe
beliefs.description: Open Word Bible's statement of faith, its vision and mission, and the values that guide the translation.
beliefs.kicker: We begin with what we believe
beliefs.heading: The faith we translate in
creed: I believe in God, the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth.

I believe in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary. He suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died and was buried; he descended to the dead. On the third day he rose again. He ascended into heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father, and he will come to judge the living and the dead.
I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and the life everlasting.
beliefs.scripture: These words are the Apostles' Creed, confessed by the church since its first centuries. We also believe that the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments are the word of God, and the final authority for faith and life.
beliefs.vision: That people from every nation, tribe and language may hear the mighty deeds of God in their own words, from a Bible anyone may use and anyone may check.
beliefs.mission: To translate the Bible from Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek into modern languages, to show the reasoning behind every sentence, and to give it all away.
values: the original languages, never another translation.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: What Open Word Bible keeps about you, and why: no ads, no tracking, and an account only if you want one.
privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.dek: You can read Open Word Bible without an account, without ads and without being tracked. This page says what we keep when you do sign in, and why.
sections: Reading without an account
We use no analytics, no advertising and no tracking cookies. Every page, font and script comes from our own site, so no other company learns what you read here.

Your reader settings, reading place, bookmarks, highlights, recent searches, reading-plan progress and the chapters you save for offline reading are kept in your own browser, not sent to us. Clearing your browser’s data for this site, or Clear this device on the account page, removes them.
Searching
A search is sent to our server to find its matches. We don’t save your searches or tie them to you, and recent searches stay in your browser.
If you create an account
An account keeps only what it needs to work:

• your email address, which is how you sign in, and a password if you choose one, stored only as a secure hash;
  • a display name, if you set one, shown to reviewers on your suggestions and questions;
  • your bookmarks and highlights (with the verse’s words as you saw them) and your reading place, so they follow you to your other devices;
  • each signed-in device: the browser’s own description of itself, when it signed in and when it was last used (signing out removes it);
  • any role you hold, such as reviewer or editor, and the review record of who approved what, and when.
Sign-in links and device keys are stored only as fingerprints that can’t be turned back into working links or keys.
Keeping sign-in safe
To stop abuse, we record each sign-in link that is asked for: the address, the time and the network (IP) address it came from. Wrong passwords are kept for an hour, to limit guessing.
If you sign in with Google, Google tells us your email address and that it has checked it. We ask for nothing else; Google’s own privacy policy covers what it records.
Who else handles your data

We don’t sell your data, share it with advertisers or use it to profile you. A few services help us run the site: Render hosts the site, the server and its database, and, like any host, keeps short-lived request logs; an email service delivers sign-in emails; and when something breaks, an error report goes to Sentry with your address, cookies, searches and the other details of the request removed.
Your choices

On your account page you can download your account details, clear this device, and delete your account. Deleting it removes your email address, display name, password, devices, bookmarks, highlights and reading place.
One exception: a reviewer’s account is kept with the review record, because the record says who approved each sentence. Ask an editor to close it.
Children
Anyone may read Open Word Bible. Accounts are meant for people aged 13 or over; if you are younger, ask a parent or guardian first.
Changes and questions
If we change how we handle data, we will update this page and the date at the top. Questions are welcome on GitHub; please don’t put personal details in a public issue.

terms_of_use.title: Terms of use
terms_of_use.description: The terms for using the Open Word Bible website and an account on it. The translation itself is in the public domain.
terms_of_use.heading: Terms of use
terms_of_use.dek: The translation is a gift: it is in the public domain. These terms cover using this website, and an account on it.
sections: The translation is yours to use

The translation, its notes, its reasoning records and its alignments are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0. You may copy, print, translate, publish and build on them without asking and without paying. Credit is welcome but not required. The website’s code is MIT-licensed.
Other people’s texts
The source texts and data, and the reference Bibles shown for comparison, belong to others and keep their own licences, listed in Sources and credits. Check those licences before you reuse them.
A draft, not yet reviewed

Every sentence is drafted with AI help and stays marked unreviewed until a named reviewer who reads the original language approves it. Drafts can be wrong. Check anything that matters against the original languages and other translations, and please report mistakes.
Your account
Sign up with an email address that is yours, keep your password and your devices secure, and use one account for one person. You can delete your account at any time from your account page.
Using the site fairly

• Don’t try to break, overload or get around the security of the site or its API.
  • Don’t pretend to be someone else, or use the site to harass, deceive or harm anyone.
  • Don’t send anything unlawful, or anything you have no right to share.
  • For the whole text, use the downloads, the API or the source on GitHub rather than scraping pages.
What you contribute

Suggestions, questions and corrections you send to the project, here or on GitHub, are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 like the rest of the translation, so that they can be used in it. Send only what you have the right to give. Your bookmarks, highlights and private notes stay yours and private.
No warranty

The site and the translation are given freely, as they are, without warranty of any kind. As far as the law allows, Open Word Bible and its contributors are not liable for any loss that comes from using them. Nothing in these terms takes away rights the law gives you that cannot be taken away.
Ending and changes

We may suspend or close an account that breaks these terms. We may also update these terms; the date at the top says when they last changed, and using the site after a change means you accept it. Questions are welcome on GitHub. How we handle your data is set out in our privacy notice.
